This rmd is a complete documentation of all of the necessary statistics performed for chapter 1 of my phd thesis (2023-2026) including data on boldness, exploration, social motivation, inhibitory control, and spatial learning.

```{r scoto_detour_morpho dataframe set up}
# load in data on boldness, exploration, social motivation, and inhibitory control
f<- "C:/Users/maxma/Downloads/scoto_detour_morpho_df.csv"

# create df with individuals that solved the detour reaching task only and set all non-learners to 600 seconds

scoto_detour_morpho_df$Treatment <- factor(
  scoto_detour_morpho_df$Treatment.x,
  levels = c("C", "L", "H"),
  labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
)

# make female and male only dfs
fdf<- scoto_detour_morpho_df |> filter(Sex.x == "F")
mdf<- scoto_detour_morpho_df |> filter(Sex.x == "M")
```

```{r route learning dataframe set up}
# load in data on spatial learning
f<- "C:/Users/maxma/Downloads/Route Learning Master Sheet_R - copy.csv"
rl_df<- read_csv(f)

# fix the time to reach transparent barriers to numeric
rl_df$latency_transparentbarrier1 <- as.numeric(rl_df$latency_transparentbarrier1)
rl_df$latency_transparent2 <- as.numeric(rl_df$latency_transparent2)


# set any numeric columns in rl_df < 0 to NA; makes all (-) data = 0 to say the event did not occur
for (col in names(rl_df)) {
  if (is.numeric(rl_df[[col]])) {
    rl_df[[col]][rl_df[[col]] < 0] <- NA
    rl_df[[col]][is.nan(rl_df[[col]])] <- NA
  }
}

# coerce all barrier choices to numeric, calculate total incorrect & correct choices & error rate over trials
rl_df <- rl_df |> 
  mutate(
    number_wrong_barrier_1 = as.numeric(as.character(number_wrong_barrier_1)),
    number_wrong_barrier_2 = as.numeric(as.character(number_wrong_barrier_2)),
    number_correct_barrier_1 = as.numeric(as.character(number_correct_barrier_1)),
    number_correct_barrier_2 = as.numeric(as.character(number_correct_barrier_2)),
    total_errors = number_wrong_barrier_1 + number_wrong_barrier_2,
    total_correct = number_correct_barrier_1 + number_correct_barrier_2,
    trial_error_rate = total_errors / (total_errors + total_correct)
  )


# set all unsolved trials to 500 in solve_2 and create dfs for stopping at trial 4 and of only trial 4
rl_df4<- rl_df|> filter(trial_num <= 4)
rl_df4_only<- rl_df|> filter(trial_num == 4)
rl_df5<- rl_df|> filter(trial_num == 5)
rl_df3<- rl_df|> filter(trial_num == 3)
rl_df2<- rl_df|> filter(trial_num == 2)
rl_df1<- rl_df|> filter(trial_num == 1)
```

```{r custom functions for heatmap}
# Function for making heatmaps of all pairwise Spearman correlations within treatments & sexes; used to measure behavioral syndromes / profiles
heatmap_maker_spearman <- function(df) {
  library(ggplot2)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(reshape2)
  library(rlang)

  numeric_df <- df[sapply(df, is.numeric)]
  var_names <- colnames(numeric_df)

  corr_mat <- matrix(NA, ncol = length(var_names), nrow = length(var_names))
  pval_mat <- matrix(NA, ncol = length(var_names), nrow = length(var_names))
  colnames(corr_mat) <- rownames(corr_mat) <- var_names
  colnames(pval_mat) <- rownames(pval_mat) <- var_names

  for (i in seq_along(var_names)) {
    for (j in seq_along(var_names)) {
      x <- numeric_df[[var_names[i]]]
      y <- numeric_df[[var_names[j]]]
      test <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))
      corr_mat[i, j] <- test$estimate
      pval_mat[i, j] <- test$p.value
    }
  }

  corr_df <- melt(corr_mat, varnames = c("Var1", "Var2"), value.name = "rho")
  pval_df <- melt(pval_mat, varnames = c("Var1", "Var2"), value.name = "p")

 heatmap_df <- left_join(corr_df, pval_df, by = c("Var1", "Var2")) %>%
  filter(as.numeric(factor(Var1, levels = var_names)) > as.numeric(factor(Var2, levels = var_names))) %>%
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      "atop(rho == ", sprintf("%.2f", rho),
      ", p == ", sprintf("%.2f", p), ")"
    ),
    p_cat = cut(p, breaks = c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1), labels = c("***", "**", "*", "")))
 
  ggplot(heatmap_df, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = rho)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(
  aes(label = label, fontface = ifelse(p < 0.05, "bold", "plain")),
  size = 3.2,
  parse = TRUE
) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#6D9EC1", mid = "white", high = "#E46726", midpoint = 0,
                         limit = c(-1, 1), name = "Spearman\nCorrelation") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
  axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
  axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
  axis.title.x = element_blank(),
  axis.title.y = element_blank(),
  panel.grid = element_blank()
) +
    coord_fixed()
}


# function to compare the correlations between two groups individually (ex. solve time distance moved correlation in control females vs relationship in control males)
compare_correlations <- function(df, 
                                 sex1, treatment1, 
                                 sex2, treatment2,
                                 var1 = Solve_Time, 
                                 var2 = Distance_moved_Total_cm) {
  
  # Capture inputs
  var1 <- enquo(var1)
  var2 <- enquo(var2)
  sex1 <- as_label(enquo(sex1))
  treatment1 <- as_label(enquo(treatment1))
  sex2 <- as_label(enquo(sex2))
  treatment2 <- as_label(enquo(treatment2))
  
  # Group 1
  group1 <- df %>%
    filter(Sex.x == sex1, Treatment.x == treatment1) %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!var1) & !is.na(!!var2))
  
  r1 <- cor(pull(group1, !!var1), pull(group1, !!var2), method = "spearman")
  n1 <- nrow(group1)
  
  # Group 2
  group2 <- df %>%
    filter(Sex.x == sex2, Treatment.x == treatment2) %>%
    filter(!is.na(!!var1) & !is.na(!!var2))
  
  r2 <- cor(pull(group2, !!var1), pull(group2, !!var2), method = "spearman")
  n2 <- nrow(group2)
  
  # Edge case check
  if (n1 < 4 | n2 < 4 | is.na(r1) | is.na(r2)) {
    return(tibble(
      sex1 = sex1, treatment1 = treatment1, r1 = r1, n1 = n1,
      sex2 = sex2, treatment2 = treatment2, r2 = r2, n2 = n2,
      z_score = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_
    ))
  }
  
  # Fisher z transform
  z1 <- 0.5 * log((1 + r1) / (1 - r1))
  z2 <- 0.5 * log((1 + r2) / (1 - r2))
  
  se_diff <- sqrt(1 / (n1 - 3) + 1 / (n2 - 3))
  z_score <- (z1 - z2) / se_diff
  p_value <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_score)))
  
  tibble(
    sex1 = sex1, treatment1 = treatment1, r1 = r1, n1 = n1,
    sex2 = sex2, treatment2 = treatment2, r2 = r2, n2 = n2,
    z_score = z_score,
    p_value = p_value
  )
}

```

```{r fdr heatmap}
heatmap_maker_spearman <- function(df) {
  library(ggplot2)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(reshape2)
  library(rlang)

  numeric_df <- df[sapply(df, is.numeric)]
  var_names <- colnames(numeric_df)

  corr_mat <- matrix(NA, ncol = length(var_names), nrow = length(var_names))
  pval_mat <- matrix(NA, ncol = length(var_names), nrow = length(var_names))
  colnames(corr_mat) <- rownames(corr_mat) <- var_names
  colnames(pval_mat) <- rownames(pval_mat) <- var_names

  for (i in seq_along(var_names)) {
    for (j in seq_along(var_names)) {
      x <- numeric_df[[var_names[i]]]
      y <- numeric_df[[var_names[j]]]
      test <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))
      corr_mat[i, j] <- test$estimate
      pval_mat[i, j] <- test$p.value
    }
  }

  corr_df <- melt(corr_mat, varnames = c("Var1", "Var2"), value.name = "rho")
  pval_df <- melt(pval_mat, varnames = c("Var1", "Var2"), value.name = "p")

  heatmap_df <- left_join(corr_df, pval_df, by = c("Var1", "Var2")) %>%
    # keep only unique pairs (lower triangle)
    filter(as.numeric(factor(Var1, levels = var_names)) >
             as.numeric(factor(Var2, levels = var_names))) %>%
    # FDR adjust across the unique tests
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
    mutate(
      label = paste0(
        "atop(rho == ", sprintf("%.2f", rho),
        ", q == ", sprintf("%.2f", p_adj), ")"   # q = FDR-adjusted p-value
      ),
      p_cat = cut(p_adj,
                  breaks = c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                  labels = c("***", "**", "*", ""))
    )

  ggplot(heatmap_df, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = rho)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = label, fontface = ifelse(p_adj < 0.05, "bold", "plain")),
      size = 3.2,
      parse = TRUE
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "#6D9EC1", mid = "white", high = "#E46726",
      midpoint = 0, limit = c(-1, 1),
      name = "Spearman\nCorrelation"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    ) +
    coord_fixed()
}
```

DETOUR REACHING TASK
```{r (NON LEARNERS) Solve Latency GLMM + dredge + estimated marginal means comparison}
# 1. build simple model df with only necessary components to reduce data loss
detour_model_df<- scoto_detour_morpho_df |> dplyr::select(fish_id, Sex.x, Treatment.x, MP_Binary, Tank_ID,Solve_Time) |> na.omit()

# 2. Build solve_time model with predictors from previous model_df (all potential predictors of solve_time)
Solve_Time_model<- glmmTMB( 
  Solve_Time ~ Treatment.x * Sex.x + (1|Tank_ID),
  data = detour_model_df,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"), na.action = na.fail
) 

# 2.1 build null model for LRT comparison
Solve_Time_null <- glmmTMB(
  Solve_Time ~ 1 + (1 | Tank_ID),
  data = detour_model_df,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  na.action = na.fail
)

anova(Solve_Time_null, Solve_Time_model)


# 3. Check model assumptions
plot(simulateResiduals(Solve_Time_model)) 

# 4. Look at summary of overall model
summary(Solve_Time_model)


# 3. use [dredge] to extract top AIC model (which predictors are most important to describing the trend of response)
m1<- dredge(Solve_Time_model)

(dredge_results<- m1)

best_model <- get.models(dredge_results, 1)[[1]]
summary(best_model) # best model includes treatment only?


# 4. Use emmeans to compare means of each group to each other
library(emmeans)
emm <- emmeans(Solve_Time_model, ~ Treatment.x | Sex.x, type = "response")
emm_males <- subset(emm, Sex.x == "M")
emm_males

pairs(emm_males, adjust = "holm")
pairs(emm, adjust = "holm")

plot(emm_males, comparisons = TRUE)

emm <- emmeans(Solve_Time_model, ~ Sex.x | Treatment.x)
pairs(emm)

```

```{r plot of solve_latency estimated marginal means}
library(emmeans)

emm <- emmeans(Solve_Time_model, ~ Treatment.x * Sex.x, type = "response")
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm)

emm_df <- emm_df |>
  dplyr::rename(
    lower.CL = asymp.LCL,
    upper.CL = asymp.UCL
  )

pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.75)

ggplot(emm_df,
       aes(x = Treatment.x,
           y = response,
           fill = Sex.x,
           group = Sex.x)) +

  geom_col(position = pd,
           width = 0.7,
           color = "black",
           alpha = 0.8) +

  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
                position = pd,
                width = 0.2,
                linewidth = 0.8) +

  labs(x = "",
       y = "Estimated mean solve latency (s)",
       fill = "Sex") +

  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    C = "Control",
    L = "Low",
    H = "High"
  )) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    Female = "#E69F00",
    Male   = "#56B4E9"
  )) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )
```

SCOTOTAXIS ASSAY
```{r beta Boldness GLMM + dredge + raw data boxplot}
# 2 Analyses will be performed here. 1.) I will use a binomial GLMM to identify if there are any mean trait differences across treatment*sex groups and a dispersion model to test whther or not some groups differed in variance.
# 2.) I will use an anova to briefly identify mean trait differences in distance moved

# Lastly I will visualize the analyses as a boxplot

# 1. Create model df with necessary components & remove NAs & 0s
model_df<- scoto_detour_morpho_df |> dplyr::select(fish_id, Sex.x, Treatment.x, Cumulative_Duration_Total_Black, Tank_ID, Distance_moved_Total_cm) |> filter(Cumulative_Duration_Total_Black>0) |> na.omit()
view(model_df)

library(glmmTMB)

# Step 2: Rescale response to (0,1)
# shrink values slightly away from 0 and 1
# scale large predictor variables
epsilon <- 1e-6
model_df$Cumulative_Duration_Total_Black_scaled <- 
  (model_df$Cumulative_Duration_Total_Black / 600) * (1 - 2*epsilon) + epsilon
model_df$Distance_moved_scaled <- scale(model_df$Distance_moved_Total_cm)


# Quick check: range should now be strictly between 0 and 1
range(model_df$Cumulative_Duration_Total_Black_scaled)

# Step 3: Fit Beta GLMM with dispformula to allow for diff sex-treatment groups to have diff variances

beta_mod2 <- glmmTMB(
  Cumulative_Duration_Total_Black_scaled ~ Treatment.x * Sex.x  +(1 | Tank_ID),
  dispformula = ~ Treatment.x * Sex.x,  # allows dispersion to vary by group
  data = model_df,
  family = beta_family(link = "logit"),
  na.action=na.fail
)

# Step 3.1: Test model assumptions

plot(simulateResiduals(beta_mod2))


summary(beta_mod2) # males have significantly HIGHER variance than females

# compare full to null model:
null <- glmmTMB(
  Cumulative_Duration_Total_Black_scaled ~ 1 + (1|Tank_ID),
  dispformula = ~1,
  data = model_df,
  family = beta_family(link = "logit")
)

anova(null, beta_mod2)


# Step 4: Dredge model 

m1<- dredge(beta_mod2)
 (dredge_results<- m1)
# Step 5: acquire best model:
best_model <- get.models(dredge_results, 1)[[1]]
summary(best_model) # significant tank variance
# males have HIGHER variance and HIGHER boldness than females
# high treatment has HIGHER variance than control
```

```{r interaction model learning slope GLMM}

library(dplyr)
library(MASS)
library(broom)
library(glmmTMB)

# organize df by fish ID so all are in order, filter out all trials where error rate is NA or there are fewer than 2 trials
rl_df4 %>%
  group_by(fish_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_trials = n(),
    n_nonNA = sum(!is.na(trial_error_rate))
  ) %>%
  filter(n_nonNA < 2)


# create df of slopes of trial error rate / trial numbers
slopes_df <- rl_df4 %>%
  group_by(fish_id) %>%
  filter(sum(!is.na(trial_error_rate)) >= 2) %>%  # need ≥2 points
  do({
    fit <- lm(trial_error_rate ~ trial_num, data = .)
    tidy_fit <- broom::tidy(fit)

    data.frame(
      slope      = tidy_fit$estimate[tidy_fit$term == "trial_num"],
      slope_SE   = tidy_fit$std.error[tidy_fit$term == "trial_num"],
      intercept  = tidy_fit$estimate[tidy_fit$term == "(Intercept)"],
      sex        = unique(.$sex),
      treatment  = unique(.$treatment),
      tank_id    = unique(.$tank_id)
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(fish_id, .keep_all = TRUE) # removes duplicates


# create model of how treatment*sex predict slope
slope_mod_var <- glmmTMB(
  slope ~ treatment * sex + (1 | tank_id),
  dispformula = ~ treatment * sex,   # allows different residual variances by group
  family = gaussian(),
  data = slopes_df
)
summary(slope_mod_var)


library(DHARMa)

sim <- simulateResiduals(slope_mod_var, n = 1000)
plot(sim)

```

```{r group level inference on learning rates + visualization}

library(emmeans)
# get group level mean slopes from glmm
emm_slopes <- emmeans(
  slope_mod_var,
  ~ treatment * sex
)

emm_slopes

# test whether group slopes are different from 0 (already applies correction)
learn_tests <- test(emm_slopes, null = 0)
learn_tests

# compare slopes between groups
pairs(emm_slopes, adjust = "holm")


emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_slopes)

ggplot(emm_df,
       aes(x = treatment, y = emmean, color = sex)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4), size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.4),
                width = 0.2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    y = "Mean learning rate\n(change in error rate per trial)",
    x = ""
  )
```

```{r Fisher's z Correlation Comparisons}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(rlang)

pairwise_correlations_all_vars <- function(df) {
  
  # variables to test = all except group identifiers
  vars <- setdiff(names(df), c("fish_id", "Sex.x", "Treatment.x"))
  
  # all pairs of variables
  var_pairs <- combn(vars, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  
  # all unique groups
  groups <- df %>%
    distinct(Sex.x, Treatment.x)
  
  # all pairwise combinations of groups
  group_pairs <- combn(1:nrow(groups), 2, simplify = FALSE)
  
  # run all tests
  results <- map_dfr(
    group_pairs,
    ~ {
      g1 <- groups[.x[1], ]
      g2 <- groups[.x[2], ]
      
      map_dfr(
        var_pairs,
        function(vp) {
          compare_correlations(
            df,
            sex1 = !!sym(as.character(g1$Sex.x)),
            treatment1 = !!sym(as.character(g1$Treatment.x)),
            sex2 = !!sym(as.character(g2$Sex.x)),
            treatment2 = !!sym(as.character(g2$Treatment.x)),
            var1 = !!sym(vp[1]),
            var2 = !!sym(vp[2])
          ) %>%
            mutate(var1 = vp[1], var2 = vp[2])
        }
      )
    }
  )
  
  results
}


all_corrs <- pairwise_correlations_all_vars(df)

print(all_corrs)
view(all_corrs)

sig_corrs <- all_corrs |> filter(p_value <0.05)
view(sig_corrs) #none are significant after bonnferroni correction
```
